newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldovan PM, govt to quit after presidential poll.
newsitem.headline: Moldovan PM, govt to quit after presidential poll.

text.p: Prime Minister Andrei Sangheli, one of the losers in Sunday's Moldovan presidential elections, said he and his cabinet would resign after the second round of the poll takes place on December 1.

"I am ready to tender my resignation after the election of a new president...to preserve peace and order in the republic," Sangheli said in a Wednesday night television address. "This is both my personal decision and that of the whole government."
President Mircea Snegur, who took first place in Sunday's first-round ballot with 39 percent of the votes, has repeatedly said that the "corrupt and incompetent" government must go.
Sangheli, who won just nine percent of the votes, joined forces on Tuesday with runner-up Petru Lucinschi and called on all leftist forces to unite around the speaker.
Parliament chairman Lucinschi, who won 28 percent of the first-round vote, competes against Snegur in the runoff.
A Lucinschi aide told Reuters that the communists, whose leader Vladimir Voronin got 10 percent in the first round, were also likely to back Lucinschi.

Snegur has called for a "nationwide front against communist and revanchist forces", but Valeriu Matei, the last possible ally left with nine percent of the first-round vote, has said he had to consult with his Party of Democratic Forces first.
Snegur and Lucinschi, both 56 and senior communists in Soviet times, offer two different visions for Moldova, a country of 4.3 million sandwiched between Romania and Ukraine.
Centre-right Snegur wants closer ties with the West and with Moldova's ethnic kin in Romania and is seeking changes in the constitution to boost presidential powers.
Left-leaning Lucinschi does not intend to amend the law and seeks equally close ties with Romania and regional power Russia, on which Moldova heavily depends for supplies of fuel and energy.
